title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary executor; the preregistered harmful-change mapping is reproduced in Methods and the per-episode raw traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json). We document the omission, provide the exact operational mapping and artifact locations for independent reproduction, and treat the preregistered harmful-overrepair claim as unresolved for confirmatory inference while preserving all other preregistered results.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in program repair and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) reports that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps report benefit for diagnostic and read-oriented assistance but caution about closed-loop autonomous changes without rigorous verification [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. A methodological risk identified in prior work is low intervention activation: verifier-guided repair can affect outcomes only when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. To address this, we use a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired design that reuses the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair architectures have empirical support in code and IaC domains where deterministic verifiers raise verifier-pass rates and supply diagnostics used for repair [1], [2]. Controlled analyses document pathologies such as verifier-exploitation and report measurable interaction costs (a "verifier tax") that affect operational feasibility [3], [4]. Survey and field studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps indicate clear value for read-oriented assistance but show limited evidence for safe closed-loop autonomous changes without deterministic checks and reconciliation [5]. These findings motivated a controlled, artifact-grounded evaluation targeted at vendor-CLI templates with explicit preregistration, deterministic fault operators, and paired shared-candidate semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where per-pair binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance agreement (verifier+simulator). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Adapter semantics, pairing, and sampling. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. For each preregistered task index (1..40) a deterministic controlled-fault candidate was produced by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1 and reused unchanged across both conditions. Exactly one initial generation per task pair was sampled and shared; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 80, completed_episode_count = 78, complete_pair_count = 39, model_calls_used = 118 (<= maximum_model_calls = 120), source_generation_attempt_count = 40, source_valid_count = 39, and source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini and temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure the intervention was meaningfully testable we preregistered deterministic controlled faults across 40 task indices that inject realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, make_before_break patterns). The controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6 is archived in the execution manifest. The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; this occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring rules and the preregistered harmful-change mapping. The primary success predicate required agreement of the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. The preregistered harmful-change mapping (used to label per-episode harmful edits for the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis) is the compact operational rule reproduced here (this exact mapping was frozen and archived in the transformation artifact): any per-episode validator violation with code PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE is labeled a harmful change for the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation. The archived per-episode validator traces include violation codes (validator_trace.violation_codes) enabling automated harmful-change aggregation. The transformation artifact manifest path is execution/transformation_manifest.json (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the full artifact hash manifest).

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial). We report discordant-pair counts, the absolute paired risk difference (guarded−baseline), a two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity was controlled by defining a single primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: (1) primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; (2) sensitivity treats missing episodes as failures. All raw per-episode artifacts and provider traces are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json) for independent recomputation.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and exclusions. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2 and both_missing_pairs = 1 (the single excluded pair resulted from an invalid/unscorable source generation). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Analysis artifacts analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv are archived and their SHA-256 hashes are recorded in the artifact manifest.

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The paired contingency CSV is archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis that guarded repair would not increase harmful over-repair by more than an absolute 5% threshold. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). The per-episode validator traces and provider traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair counts are archived at execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. The preregistered harmful-change mapping (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE → harmful-change) is reproduced above and archived in execution/transformation_manifest.json. Because the archived confirmatory executor did not produce the preregistered aggregated harmful-overrepair artifact and aggregated counts are not present in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not retroactively present a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair claim in this paper; rather we (a) document the omission, (b) provide the exact mapping and artifact locations needed for automated reproduction, and (c) label any future counts computed outside the archived confirmatory summary as exploratory. Reproduction instructions: aggregate over complete pairs the indicator harmful_change = any(validator_trace.validation_after.violation_codes ∩ {"PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE","UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE"} ≠ ∅) per condition, then compute paired counts and exact paired inference per the preregistered analysis plan. The required raw traces and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping are archived and auditable.

Representative artifact-grounded diagnostics. We present three representative pairs (artifact-grounded examples available in execution/scoring/) to illustrate typical verifier-guided corrections and the kinds of faults injected. (All example JSON artifacts are archived and their SHA-256s are recorded in the manifest.)

- Pair task-000001 (dropped_required_restore pattern): shared controlled-fault candidate normalized_configuration = "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600". Baseline repaired candidate validated as valid after repair (validation_after.valid = true) and had no harmful violation codes; guarded repair also succeeded and the archived guarded trace records validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true.

- Pair task-000002 (protected_interface_change pattern): the shared candidate included a change to protected interface mgmt1; baseline validation_after.violation_codes included ["PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE","UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE","FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH"] (thus mapping to harmful-change per preregistered rule), while the guarded repair removed those violations and validated as valid after repair.

- Pair task-000003 (paired_link_atomic_mtu_change pattern): baseline left PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations after repair (validation_after.violation_codes included PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE) and failed validation; the guarded repair removed those violations and produced a valid configuration. Full JSON traces for these examples are archived (execution/scoring/task-00000{1,2,3}-*.json) and cited in the artifact manifest.

Exploratory instrumentation and cost accounting. Stage-level instrumentation recorded stage_counts = {valid_source_generation: 40, blind_controlled_fault_repair: 39, validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair: 39} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 118. These counts permit exploratory cost-per-outcome calculations (model_call_cost_per_avoided_failure) using archived provider billing or cost-per-call metadata if available to an auditor; we present stage and call counts here as descriptive artifacts and label any monetary or latency cost calculations as exploratory because large-scale operational feasibility requires broader study.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and causal scope. Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points). The shared-candidate paired design isolates the causal effect of diagnostic exposure because each arm received the same controlled-fault candidate, identical repair budgets, and identical model identity and sampling budget constraints.

Unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic was not present in the archived confirmatory summary executor output; reconstructing it is straightforward from the archived per-episode validator_trace.violation_codes and the reproduced harmful-change mapping, but that aggregation was not computed by the archived confirmatory summary. Therefore we do not present a preregistered confirmatory safety verdict here. We provide the exact mapping and the artifact locations needed for independent reproduction so auditors can compute the preregistered counts and paired inference without additional model calls.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity — prompt sensitivity and nondeterministic hosted-model sampling (temperature = null/unset) limit claims about deterministic first-pass generation; exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was performed and reused under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, so paired differences reflect only diagnostic exposure and subsequent repair calls. Construct validity — primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity is an important construct limitation. External validity — single-model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic, deterministic controlled-fault task bank limit generalization to heterogeneous production workloads. Conclusion validity — n = 39 complete pairs yields reasonable power for the observed effect size but limits precision for subgroup inference and fault-class stratification. Operational feasibility — instrumented hosted-model call counts are archived; assessing the verifier tax at operational scale requires larger deployments and cost/latency traces beyond this confirmatory scope.

Operational implications and mitigations. The finding supports the value of deterministic verifier diagnostics as a repair cue in controlled challenge conditions, but production adoption should consider multi-verifier ensembles, calibrated abstention, and explicit harmful-change labeling to limit over-repair risk and verifier-exploitation. The artifact bundle includes per-episode evidence required to evaluate harmful-change rates and to test mitigation strategies without additional model calls.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used here. A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered statistic. We release the artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in execution manifest = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE → harmful-change; see execution/transformation_manifest.json and the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
